chunks.content:
Studio, your agent, and the CLI work on the same project files. Use **Code** for
a small source change you understand. Use the agent when the change crosses
files, affects project structure, or starts from an unfamiliar failure.

| Change                                                           | Best starting point            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Visible text, layout, style, media, timing, or supported motion  | Canvas, Inspector, or timeline |
| One known value in one known file                                | Code                           |
| Story, several scenes, generated animation, or project structure | Agent                          |
| A reported lint problem with a clear direct fix                  | Studio or Code                 |
| An unfamiliar failure or a fix spanning files                    | Copy to Agent                  |

The choice is about the change, not a permanent workflow. You can move between
the surfaces without exporting or converting the project.

1. Open **Code** in the left panel column.
2. Select the exact file in the project tree.
3. Find the value responsible for the visible result.
4. Make one focused change.
5. Wait for the preview to refresh, then play the affected moment.

The Code editor saves user edits automatically and records them in Studio
history. If a save fails, Studio says that the latest edit was not persisted;
fix the preview-server or connection problem before continuing.

<Warning>
  Creating, renaming, moving, or deleting a file can break references elsewhere in the project.
  Search for the old path or ask the agent to update every reference.
</Warning>

Avoid editing the same file in Studio and another tool at the same time. If an
external change lands first, the Code editor rejects the conflicting save and
tells you that the latest edit was not persisted. Reload the current file,
review the external change, then apply your edit again. The separate queue for
visual canvas edits can pause and show a banner while a conflict is resolved.

When a visible element needs source work, select it and choose **Ask agent about this element**. Studio prepares the element and project context, combines it with your instruction, and copies the prompt to the clipboard. Paste that prompt into your agent chat. ```text Keep the current narration and scene order. Make this product panel readable at the final video size, and do not change the following scene. ``` The copied context tells the agent where to look. Your sentence tells it what must remain true.

Choose **Lint** at the bottom of the left panel column. Studio opens **HyperFrame
Lint Results** with errors, warnings, file locations, and fix hints when they
are available.

Fix a simple, understood issue directly, then run Lint again. Use **Copy to
Agent** when the source location is unfamiliar or the fix may affect other
files. Add what happened before the error and what you expected:

```text
This appeared after I shortened the intro clip. I expected the title animation
to keep its current timing. Fix the issue without changing the rest of the
opening.
```

Do not paste only the error message when the intended result matters. A
technically valid repair can still make the wrong creative change.

chunks.section_title: Use the project-level gates before delivery
chunks.content:
Studio Lint is a quick in-editor pass. The project-level commands remain the
final gate, especially when the project contains nested compositions:

```bash
npx hyperframes lint
npx hyperframes check
```

`lint` checks the composition structure. `check` adds browser, runtime, layout,
motion, and WCAG contrast verification.

Passing checks do not approve the story or the final encode. Play the project
after a source fix, then watch the rendered file before sharing it.

chunks.section_title: When the preview and source disagree
chunks.content:
1. Stop editing until the latest save finishes.
2. Keep the first exact error or save warning.
3. Reload the project only after checking whether another tool changed the file.
4. Run the project checks.
5. Ask the agent with the error, project path, action that caused it, and result
   you expected.

Use [Studio troubleshooting](/studio/troubleshooting) for editor, preview, and
render-queue failures. Use [Finish and share](/guides/export-and-share) for the
complete approval, validation, render, and delivery path.

- [Recover from a Studio problem](/studio/troubleshooting)
- [Understand a HyperFrames project](/concepts)
- [Finish, render, and share](/guides/export-and-share)

documents.title: Edit timing on the timeline
documents.summary: Move, trim, split, align, and inspect clips in HyperFrames Studio.
documents.rights_reason: External unvendored media hosted on remote HeyGen CDN

chunks.content: The timeline controls when elements appear and how long they remain.

Drag the body of a clip left or right. Its start time changes while its duration stays the same.

Use snapping to align the clip with the playhead, another boundary, or a useful beat.

Drag the left or right edge.

- Trimming the left edge changes when the clip begins.
- Trimming the right edge changes when it ends.

Trimming does not automatically rewrite the story. Play the surrounding section to check entrances, exits, media continuity, and narration.

Splitting is supported for eligible timeline elements.

You can:

- place the playhead, open the clip menu, and choose **Split at…**;
- switch to the razor tool and click the clip;
- hold Shift while using the razor to split every eligible clip under that time.

Use the **B** shortcut to switch to the razor tool. Return to the selection tool when you finish cutting.

<Note>
  A split must happen inside the clip, not exactly on its start or end. Some element types cannot be split safely.
</Note>

Zoom in for keyframes and short edits. Zoom out to understand the complete sequence.

Use the playhead for the exact edit moment. Use playback and frame stepping to check what happens immediately before and after it.

Tab into the timeline to reach its current logical focus target. Use Left and Right to move within that row. Use Up and Down to move to the nearest target at the same time in the previous or next row.

Home and End move to the start or end of the focused row. Hold Command or Ctrl to move to the first or last logical row. Page Up and Page Down move by one visible page of rows.

On an expandable track row, Right expands collapsed keyframe property lanes and Left collapses expanded lanes. From a keyframe property row, Left returns to its parent track row. Enter or Space toggles the same lanes. Use the Context Menu key or Shift + F10 to open the focused target's menu when it has one.

The timeline keeps only one logical timeline target in the Tab order. Native header controls, such as visibility and keyframe actions, remain separate Tab stops. When the logical target is outside the virtualized viewport, Studio keeps it mounted, scrolls it into view, and then restores focus.

Screen readers receive the timeline as a treegrid. Track rows announce their level and expanded state. Clips and keyframes announce their names, times, and selection state. Easing controls announce their names and times.

See [Keyboard shortcuts](/studio/shortcuts#timeline-navigation) for the complete command table.
Beat markers provide timing landmarks, especially for music-driven work. Snap edits to them when the audio should drive the cut; ignore them when the story or voiceover needs a different rhythm.
Select multiple eligible timeline elements when they need to remain aligned. Drag them together, then check for collisions or gaps on their tracks.
Expand a nested composition to see its children, or open it and use the breadcrumb to return. Be clear whether you are changing the scene’s internal timing or its timing in the parent video.
Move, trim, split, and many other timeline actions participate in Studio history. Undo immediately when a result is unexpected, then retry with a closer zoom or a more precise playhead position.

- [Edit the frame](/studio/canvas)
- [Edit animation and keyframes](/studio/animation)
- [Use Studio keyboard shortcuts](/studio/shortcuts)

chunks.section_title: I cannot select the right element
chunks.content:
- Pause on a frame where it is visible.
- Choose it from Layers.
- Check whether it belongs to a group or nested composition.
- Look for an off-canvas indicator.

The selected element may be generated, nested, or unsupported for that operation.

Try the inspector, open the nested composition, copy context to the agent, or make a focused source edit.
Check whether auto-keyframing is enabled. Undo the edit, turn it off, and make the layout change again.

chunks.section_title: The timeline edit landed at the wrong time
chunks.content: Undo, zoom in, place the playhead more precisely, and retry. Check whether snapping moved the boundary to a nearby clip or beat.

- Preview's Code editor and visual controls save automatically. If the change came
  from another editor or an agent, confirm that the external file was saved.
- Wait for the project refresh.
- Check the terminal running `hyperframes preview`.
- Reload Studio if the preview process is still healthy.
- Restart `npx hyperframes preview` when the server stopped.
Confirm that the file exists inside the project and that its path is correct. Large media may need time to prepare a preview. Remote files can fail because of access or cross-origin restrictions.
Keep the error visible, avoid stacking more edits on top of it, and undo if available. Copy the issue to your agent with the action that caused it.

Keep the complete error. Run the project checks, confirm FFmpeg and source media are available, then retry:

```bash
npx hyperframes lint
npx hyperframes check
```

For lower-level failures, continue to [general troubleshooting](/guides/troubleshooting).

- [Work with source and an agent](/studio/source)
- [Finish, render, and share](/guides/export-and-share)
- [Diagnose a project or CLI problem](/guides/troubleshooting)

documents.title: Use variables and templates
documents.summary: Turn a visible value into a reusable input, preview variants, and hand the template off.
documents.rights_reason: External unvendored media hosted on remote HeyGen CDN

chunks.content: Variables let one project produce many versions without rebuilding its layout or animation.

The quickest path starts from the canvas:

1. Select the element.
2. Open **Variables** in the right panel.
3. Bind the text, media source, text color, background, or font property.
4. Create a new variable or choose a compatible existing one.

For a value that is not tied to the selected element, click **Add variable**. Studio supports string, number, color, boolean, enum, font, and image variables. Number variables can include minimum, maximum, and step values; enums can define their allowed options.

Name the input by meaning—`customerName`, `headline`, or `brandColor`—rather than by its position in the design.

Change a value in the Variables panel to preview that version immediately. The preview is an override: it does not replace the saved default.

The panel tells you whether you are previewing defaults or custom values. Use **Reset** to clear all preview overrides. When a scalar preview should become the new default, use **Set default**.

<Note>
  Variables from other compositions are listed separately. You can edit their declarations, but
  their values are not live-previewed in the active composition.
</Note>

At the bottom of the panel, **Use this template** can copy either:

- the effective values as JSON;
- a ready-to-run `npx hyperframes render ... --variables ...` command.

This keeps the values you just reviewed attached to the render request instead of asking the next person to reconstruct them.

- [Understand the variables contract](/concepts/variables)
- [Use Assets and Catalog](/studio/assets-and-blocks)
- [Render variable-driven versions](/guides/rendering#batch-and-cloud-work)

documents.title: Make music sit under narration
documents.summary: Take only the frequencies a voice occupies out of a music bed, so the music keeps its character while speech stays intelligible.
documents.rights_reason: Contains explicit proprietary or unreleased restriction

chunks.content:
Music under narration is the most common audio problem in a video, and the
obvious fix is the wrong one.

Turning the whole music track down works, and it costs the music all of its
presence for as long as anyone is talking — the bed goes limp through the entire
voiceover. But a voice does not need the whole spectrum. It needs the few bands it
actually occupies. A **carve** takes only those out of the music, so the bed keeps
its low end and its top: still music, while the voice stays intelligible.

Whenever a music bed plays under speech. It is not a polish step to reach if
there is time — place both tracks, carve, and listen.

Skip it only when there is no narration for the music to sit under: a music video,
a title card, a montage cut to the track.

The carve is a module at the top of the **music** track's rack, not a separate
tool. Select the music clip, open its **Audio FX** section, and the module asks
you to pick the voices this bed should make room for.

A bed with exactly one candidate voice above it is **already carved**, at the
default strength, because that is what a bed under narration wants. Several
candidates leaves the picker waiting rather than guessing which one is the voice.

<Warning>
  The carve belongs on the **music**, never on the voice. It names the tracks it
  makes room for, the same way a sidechain compressor does — you select the track
  that gets quieter and pick what makes it quieter. A voice carved against itself
  is a bug, not a subtle mix choice.
</Warning>

One control does the whole job. It derives how deep to cut, how many bands, how
wide they are, how far the level may drop, and how far under the voice to aim —
because those move together in any real mix.

| Strength | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| Default (0.25) | A 6 dB dip in three bands — audible without sounding like a hole |
| Around 0.5 | The dip reaches 10 dB, where a carve starts being heard as an effect |
| Higher | Deliberate territory for a loud bed under a quiet voice |
| 0 | Spectral only — one band, no level matching at all |

**Switch the carve off** keeps the settings and stops the carve, which is
different from clearing it: a bed with one candidate voice would otherwise be
carved again by default the moment it was re-evaluated.

Ordinary effects. Open the rack after carving and you will find a few `peaking`
filters and a `gain` stage — nothing hidden, nothing proprietary.

Two things follow from that:

- **The envelopes are editable.** The carve always follows the speech, so every
  value becomes an automation lane you can adjust by hand afterwards. Silence
  leaves the music alone; a loud passage pushes the carve to full depth. There is
  no fixed-depth mode, because a fixed dip thins the bed through every pause.
- **Re-carving is safe.** The nodes a carve writes are tagged as its own, so
  running it again at a new strength replaces exactly those and leaves every
  effect and lane you built by hand where it was.

Inside a carved bed the signal runs through the dips first, then the level match,
then anything you added yourself — which is why a limiter you place stays the last
ceiling.

chunks.section_title: Point it at a group, not at clips
chunks.content:
If narration arrives as several clips, [group them](/studio/audio-groups) and
carve against the group.

A carve pointed at individual clips has to list every one of them, and it stays
right only until the next edit: add a fourth narration clip and it plays outside
the carve's awareness, so the music silently fails to duck under it. A carve
pointed at a group resolves membership every time the analysis runs, so a clip
added later is covered without touching the carve.

Studio does this for you when you pick a second ungrouped voice — it creates a
group behind them and points the carve at that instead.

- The voice is legible without the bed sounding hollowed out.
- The music comes **back up between phrases** rather than staying flat.
- The bed keeps its bass and its top end. A carve that removed those would just
  be a filter.

**The music sounds notched or hollow.** Strength is too high. Come back toward
the default. This is the one failure mode with an obvious sound.

**The voice is still buried.** A carve cannot fix a bed that is simply louder than
the voice — spectral room does not solve a level problem. Compare the two tracks'
actual loudness first. Machine-generated speech commonly arrives far below a
mastered music track, and that gap is arithmetic rather than taste.

**The bed starts out already ducked.** A lane holds its first value backwards to
the start of its clip. A bed that begins before the voice needs an explicit "no
cut" point at its start.

**The music pumps.** The level envelope releases slowly on purpose, because music
that snaps back the instant a word ends sounds like a machine doing it. If it
still pumps, the gaps between phrases are shorter than the release — lower the
strength rather than fighting the envelope.

**Nothing was carved.** The picker leaves itself alone when several tracks could
be the voice. Name the voice explicitly.

- [Mix audio and apply effects](/studio/audio-effects)
- [Group tracks, mute, and solo](/studio/audio-groups)
- [Audio effects implementation](/reference/audio-effects#voiceover-carve)

documents.title: Connect your agent
documents.summary: Set up Claude Code or Codex once so the HyperFrames Studio app can build and change your videos.

code_references.snippet:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

# Sign in
claude auth login

documents.rights_reason: References OpenAI ChatGPT proprietary brand marks

chunks.content:
The app makes your videos with an agent that runs on your computer: **Claude Code** or **Codex**. You set one up
once. After that, every request you send goes to it.

| Agent | You need |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | A Claude account or an Anthropic Console account. The app installs it for you. |
| Codex | A ChatGPT account. You install it and sign in with two commands. |

Runs bill to the plan of the account your agent is signed in with. To use an API key instead, change **Bill runs
to** in **Settings** > **Permissions**.

If both are ready and you have not picked one, the app uses Claude Code.

The first time you send a request without an agent, the **Connect Claude Code** screen opens with three steps.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Install Claude Code">
    Choose **Install Claude Code**, then **Install** in the dialog. The app runs Anthropic's official installer,
    which puts Claude Code in your home folder. It takes about a minute.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Sign in">
    Choose **Sign in to Claude**. Your browser opens Claude's sign-in. Use your Claude account or an Anthropic Console
    account, then come back to the app.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Check that it answers">
    The app checks that Claude Code runs. When it shows **Claude Code is connected**, it sends the request you
    started with.
  </Step>
</Steps>

If a step fails, the app shows a command you can run yourself. Choose **Copy command**, then **Open Terminal**, and
paste it:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

claude auth login
```

The app does not install Codex for you. Open **Settings** > **Agent** or the agent picker in the chat header, find
Codex, and use its buttons:

1. **Copy install command**, then paste it into a terminal:
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh
   ```
2. **Copy sign-in command** (`codex`), run it in a terminal, and sign in with your ChatGPT account.
3. Back in the app, choose **Check again**. Codex shows **Ready**.

Use the agent picker in the chat header, or **Settings** > **Agent**, and choose **Use** next to the agent you want.
The choice applies to your next request.

Each agent row shows its state: **Ready**, **Not signed in**, **Not installed**, or **Installed, but won't start**,
with the button that fixes it.

- [Make your first video](/studio-app/first-video)
- [Updates and troubleshooting](/studio-app/troubleshooting)

documents.title: Change your video with the agent
documents.summary: Type a change, point at the picture, draw, or comment, then send several edits to the agent at once.
documents.rights_reason: Open Apache-2.0 / MIT motion design technique, zero proprietary asset dependencies

chunks.content: Every change starts the same way: show the agent where, say what, and send. You can type, point at something in the picture, draw over it, or leave a comment at a moment in the video.

Type in the chat box, which says **Describe a change**, and press Enter. Type `@` to add moments, media, files, or
other projects to your message.

While the agent is working, Enter queues your message to run next. To change that, open **Settings** > **Agent**
and switch **While Framey works, Send** from **Queue** to **Steer**, which stops the run and starts again with your
words. Picks and files always queue.

chunks.section_title: Point, draw, or comment on the picture
chunks.content:
The tools under the picture, on the left:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Select** (V) | Click an element, choose **Prompt to edit** (or press A), and describe the change. Click again to pick what contains it. |
| **Draw** (D) | Circle or mark a spot and say what should change. Several strokes become one drawing. |
| **Comment** (C) | Pin a comment to a spot and moment: **What should change here?** |

The picture opens with **Draw**. Press Escape to go back to **Select**. Right-click an element for quick actions
such as **Ask Framey**, **Hide**, **Bring to front**, **Replace with**, and **Delete**.

You can also draw across the timeline to talk about a stretch of the video, such as "tighten this part".

Picks, drawings, and comments do not run on their own. Each one becomes a row in **Pending video edits**, up to 10.
Check them, add a note for all of them, then send them as one request with the send button, for example
**Send 3 edits to Claude Code**. Choose **Edit note** to change a row's words, or **Delete** to drop it.

Some changes are faster by hand. Hover a clip on the timeline to **Split** it at the playhead, **Delete** it, or
open **Quick edit** to change a video or audio clip's **Speed**, **Volume**, and **Fade**. Drag clips to move or trim
them.

Right-click an empty gap for **Close gap**, or to ask what should fill it. The app suggests ideas that fit what
plays around the gap.

**Get inspired** is a library of short example moments from real videos: **Motion graphics**, **A-roll Cuts**,
and **Mobile Ads**. Find it on Home, in a new project's empty chat, and in the **Inspirations** tab beside your files.
Choose **Add** or **Use** to put a moment in your message as a reference, then say how to use it and send.
Press Cmd+Z to undo and Cmd+Shift+Z to redo (Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z on Linux). Each agent run in the chat also has its own **Undo** button.

- [Export and share](/studio-app/export)
- [Make your first video](/studio-app/first-video)
- [Updates and troubleshooting](/studio-app/troubleshooting)

documents.title: Export your video
documents.summary: Render a finished video file from the HyperFrames Studio app and find it in your Downloads folder.
documents.rights_reason: Open Apache-2.0 / MIT motion design technique, zero proprietary asset dependencies

chunks.content: When the video is ready, choose **Export** in the project's top bar. The **Export** panel opens beside the picture.

| Choice | Options | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Quality** | **1080p** or **Project size**, plus **4K** when the project fits it | 1080p |
| **Format** | **MP4**, **WebM**, **MOV** | MP4 |
| **Frame rate** | 24, 30, 60 | 30 |

MP4 is the right choice for sharing and uploading. Pick another format only when the place you are sending it asks
for one.

Choose the render button, for example **Render 1080p MP4**. The panel shows **Getting ready**, then **Rendering**
with the frames done so far, then **Finishing the file**. You can close the panel and keep working; the render
continues. Choose **Cancel** to stop it.

**Export** is unavailable while the agent is building the project. Wait for the run to finish.

The video is saved to your **Downloads** folder, named after the project with the date and time, for example
`Spring Launch 2026-05-04 10.30.mp4`. When it is done, the panel shows **Export ready** with the file size:

- **Open video** plays it.
- **Show in Finder** (**Show in folder** on Linux) opens the folder.

Watch the exported file once from start to end before you send it.

- The render fails or does not start: choose the render button again. If it keeps failing,
  ask the agent to check the project, then export again.
- **The video was made but could not be saved to your Downloads folder**: free up space or check that the Downloads
  folder exists, then export again.
- **HyperFrames could not start its built-in FFmpeg**: the app may be damaged. Reinstall it from
  [hyperframes.dev/studio](https://hyperframes.dev/studio).

- [Change your video with the agent](/studio-app/edit-with-the-agent)

documents.title: Make your first video
documents.summary: Pick four parts, add your website or idea, and let the agent build your first video in the HyperFrames Studio app.
documents.rights_reason: Open Apache-2.0 / MIT motion design technique, zero proprietary asset dependencies

chunks.content: The **Create your first video** card on Home builds a launch video from four parts, each taken from a real launch video. You pick the parts, add your website or an idea, and the agent builds one video from them. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Hook** | Grab attention in the first seconds | | **Proof** | Show the product doing its job | | **Turn** | Flip from problem to answer | | **Call to action** | Land the brand and the ask |

<Steps>
  <Step title="Pick the four parts">
    The card starts with one clip in each part. Use the shuffle button beside them for a new set, or hover a part to
    shuffle it or browse the others.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add your website or idea">
    Type your website, such as `yourcompany.com`, or describe your idea. A website gives the agent your fonts, colors
    and logo.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Choose Use this cut">
    The request goes straight to the agent. If you are not signed in or have no agent yet, the app walks you through
    that first, then sends it.
  </Step>
</Steps>

The app creates a project for your video and the agent starts building it. On your first video, a short tour
replays how a launch video was made while yours builds, then Framey takes you to your project. In the project, the
chat shows what the agent is doing, such as **Reading files** or **Editing files**.

When the agent finishes, the video is ready to play, change, and export.

projects, or media. To open the card again later, choose **Take the step by step** next to **Get inspired**.

chunks.content: The HyperFrames Studio app for Mac and Linux is the easiest way to make a video with HyperFrames. You describe the video, an agent on your computer builds it, and you change it by typing, pointing at the picture, drawing, or commenting. You do not need to write code. Framey, the small green guide, points you to the next step along the way.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Mac">
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Download">
        Go to [hyperframes.dev/studio](https://hyperframes.dev/studio) and choose **Download for macOS**.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Install">
        Open the downloaded disk image and double-click **Install HyperFrames**. The installer copies the app into
        Applications and shows **Checking it is really from HeyGen**, which can take a minute or two. When it says
        **HyperFrames is in Applications**, choose **Open HyperFrames**.
      </Step>
    </Steps>

    If your Mac's Applications folder is locked for your account, the installer puts the app in the Applications
    folder inside your home folder instead. If it says **The download looks damaged**, choose **Download again**. If
    it says the check **took too long**, nothing was installed: choose **Try again**.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Linux">
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Download">
        Go to [hyperframes.dev/studio](https://hyperframes.dev/studio) and choose **Download** next to Linux. You get
        one file, `HyperFrames-x86_64.AppImage`, for 64-bit Intel and AMD computers.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Make it runnable and open it">
        In a terminal, in the folder you downloaded it to:

        ```bash
        chmod +x HyperFrames-x86_64.AppImage
        ./HyperFrames-x86_64.AppImage
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>

    The AppImage is the whole app. Keep it anywhere you like and open it the same way next time.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

1. A short survey asks what you want to make and which agent you use. Every answer is optional, and **Skip all**
   counts as an answer. What you make decides where **Get inspired** opens. The agent you name starts your first
   chat if it is already set up.
2. Home opens with the **Create your first video** card. See
   [Make your first video](/studio-app/first-video).

A notice also explains what usage data the app records. Choose **Got it** to dismiss it.

On first launch, the app asks you to sign in the first time you click something after the survey.

1. Choose **Continue with HeyGen**. Your browser opens hyperframes.dev.
2. Sign in there within two minutes. The browser sends you back to the app, which shows **You're in!** and carries
   on with what you clicked.

If the sign-in runs out of time, choose **Continue with HeyGen** again. If you choose **Not now**, the app asks
again on your next click.
You can sign in or out at any time from **Settings** > **Account**.

- [Connect your agent](/studio-app/connect-your-agent)
- [Make your first video](/studio-app/first-video)
- [Updates and troubleshooting](/studio-app/troubleshooting)

documents.title: Updates and troubleshooting
documents.summary: How the HyperFrames Studio app updates itself, and what to do when it says your agent is signed out, out of usage, or blocked.
documents.rights_reason: Open Apache-2.0 / MIT motion design technique, zero proprietary asset dependencies

chunks.content:
The app checks for a new version when it opens and every few minutes after that. When one is ready, you get a
notification, a round update button appears in the bottom-right corner, and Framey points at it: **There's a new
update. Click here**.

1. Click the update button. It fills up as the update downloads.
2. The app restarts by itself as soon as nothing is running: no agent run, export, or setup in progress. It reopens
   the project you had open, and you do not lose anything.

To check by hand, open **Settings** > **Updates** and choose **Check for updates**. On a Mac, **HyperFrames** >
**Check for Updates…** in the menu bar does the same. Some updates show a short video of what is new.

If an update says **The update is taking longer than it should** or **The update didn't finish**, click the update
button and choose **Try again** to cancel it and start a new one, or **Download it instead** to get the
latest version from the download page. **Download the latest version** in **Settings** > **Updates** also opens the
download page. If it says **Could not check for updates**, check
your internet connection, then try again.

chunks.section_title: The app asks me to sign in to HyperFrames
chunks.content:
Sending a request needs your HeyGen account. Choose **Continue with HeyGen** and finish in your browser within two
minutes. If you see **No connection**, check your internet. If you see **The sign-in expired** or **HeyGen didn't
sign you in**, choose **Try again**.

chunks.section_title: You're signed out of Claude Code
chunks.content:
The chat shows a sign-in card. Your message is kept. Choose **Sign in**, finish in your browser, and the message
sends as soon as you are back. Choose **Use Codex instead** to send it with Codex if Codex is ready.

For Codex, the chat says **Codex is not signed in**. Choose **Copy sign-in command**, run it in a terminal, then
choose **Try again**.

chunks.section_title: My agent hit its usage limit
chunks.content:
The chat says, for example, **Claude Code hit its usage limit. It resets** at a time. This is your agent's own plan
limit, not a HyperFrames one. Wait until it resets and choose **Try again**, or choose **Switch to Codex** (or
**Switch to Claude Code**) if the other agent is set up.

If the chat says the agent **had a problem on its side**, the agent's service is busy or down. Try again in a few
minutes.

**Agent access** in **Settings** > **Agent** decides what Claude Code may do:

- **Full access**, the default: it can install, use the internet, and run anything, with no checks.
- **Auto**: it works in your project and blocks risky steps on its own.

With **Auto**, a step Claude Code refuses shows as blocked in the run's work log. If the change needed that step,
switch to **Full access** and send the request again.

chunks.section_title: The agent is not installed or won't start
chunks.content:
The chat says Claude Code **is not installed**. Choose **Try again** and the app sets it up for you. If
Claude Code is installed but will not start, choose **Reinstall** in **Settings** > **Permissions**. See
[Connect your agent](/studio-app/connect-your-agent) for the manual commands.

| The chat says | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| **… ran out of room in this chat** | Choose **Start a fresh session**. |
| **… needs an update to use** a model | Choose the update button in the chat. |
| **… could not reach the internet** | Check your connection, then **Try again**. |
| **… could not finish this change** | Choose **Try again**, or say the change differently. |

- **Your projects**: the hidden `.hyperframes-studio` folder in your home folder.
- **Exported videos**: your Downloads folder.
- **App settings and sign-in**: `Library/Application Support/HyperFrames` in your home folder on a Mac, and
  `.config/HyperFrames` in your home folder on Linux.

Each project is a plain HyperFrames project folder, so it also opens in the
[Studio web editor](/studio/index) and with the [command line](/developers/cli).

- [Connect your agent](/studio-app/connect-your-agent)
- [Export your video](/studio-app/export)
